answer: In an agent economy, requiring each new identity to post a timber bond of refundable capital before participating creates a real cost barrier. An attacker spawning many fakes must lock substantial funds per clone, and any detected Sybil loses that bond. Honest agents treat the bond as a relic of proven reliability that grows trust over time, while a quiet whisper of verified work history spreads among peers, making mass forgery unprofitable without heavy capital outlay.
